 Judgment
Challenging the dismissal of his petition for divorce, the petitioner in M.C.No.25/2014 on the file of Sr. Civil Judge and JMFC, Malavalli, has preferred this appeal.
2. The appellant was the petitioner and the respondent in this appeal was the respondent in M.C.No.25/2014 before the Trial Court.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties are referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Trial Court.
3. The marriage of the petitioner and the respondent was solemnized on 06.06.2004 at Shree Lakshmi Narasimhaswamy Temple, Marehalli, Malavalli as per Hindu rites and customs.
During their wedlock, they begot one son.
It is alleged that the respondent - wife was arrogant and nagging the petitioner and his family members for trivial matters.
The petitioner was hoping that the respondent being educated and a teacher at Government school would correct herself.
However, she continued infliction of cruelty on the petitioner.

It is further alleged that the respondent is in the habit of going to her parent's house, stay there for long and would return to the matrimonial home only after the insistence of the petitioner, stay for some time and again go to her parent's house.
It is also alleged that ever since the marriage, the respondent has subjected the petitioner to all kinds of mental torture and never discharged her duties expected of a dutiful Hindu wife.
It is contended that the respondent never respected his parents and other family members.
Their lives became miserable due to her acts.
Ultimately, in April 2011, the respondent left the matrimonial home and started residing with her parents.

Thereafter, she lodged a false complaint on 04.05.2011 which was registered as Crime No.57/2011 for the offences punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
The jurisdictional Court acquitted the petitioner and his family members on 26.08.2013 after a full fledged trial.

It is further contended that from the last week of April 2011, the respondent is residing with her parents and there is absolutely no physical relationship between them for a period of more than 3 years.
The respondent is drawing a salary of Rs.15,000/- p.m.
It is also contended that it is impossible for the petitioner to continue the marital relationship with the respondent and their marriage has been broken down irrevocably.
Hence, he sought decree of divorce on the grounds of cruelty and desertion.
4. The respondent objected the petition denying the allegations of cruelty and desertion.

It is contended that the petitioner and his family members looked after the respondent properly till the Sri M N Ravikumar vs Smt Ningamma on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105862545/
2 birth of the male child.

sentences.text: Subsequently, they did not co
- operate with the respondent in leading a peaceful marital life with the petitioner.
The petitioner also used to listen to the words of the family members and quarrel with the respondent.
It is further contended that due to the misunderstanding created by the family members of the petitioner between her and the petitioner, the marital life of the respondent has been affected.
Even now, the respondent is willing to lead marital life with the petitioner and is not willing to give divorce.
She sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. The Trial Court recorded the evidence of the parties.
The petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and on his behalf got marked Exs.P1 to P6.
The respondent got examined herself as RW-1 and also examined two witnesses as RW-2 and RW-3 but no documents were marked.

The Trial Court, on appreciation of the evidence, came to the conclusion that absolutely no evidence was placed by the petitioner to prove that the respondent deserted and neglected him without discharging her marital duties as a dutiful wife.
It is further observed that the petitioner failed to prove the grounds of cruelty and dismissed the petition.

6. Smt.M.V.Thanuja, learned counsel appearing for Sri.Thejas N.S., learned counsel for the appellant, reiterating the grounds of appeal, submits that the respondent filed a false criminal complaint against the petitioner, his mother, sister-in- law and brother, and all were honourably acquitted of the charges levelled against them.

It is submitted that RWs-1 to 3 have falsely deposed that the petitioner and his family members were acquitted in the criminal case due to a compromise with the respondent which is factually incorrect.

It is further submitted that on the basis of the false complaint lodged by the respondent, a departmental enquiry was conducted against the petitioner and he has been exonerated from the charges levelled against him.
She submits that filing of false criminal complaint amounted to cruelty.
It is also submitted that the respondent left the matrimonial home in April 2011 and thereafter she filed a false criminal complaint.
If the respondent really intended to continue the marital life, she would not have filed the criminal complaint against the petitioner.
Hence, her evidence cannot be looked into.

It is contended that the petitioner's son is now aged about 19 years and the petitioner is taking care of all his needs and his educational expenses but the respondent being a teacher, failed to take care of the petitioner and the son by deserting them.
It is further contended that the Trial Court has committed an error in appreciating the evidence available on record.
In view of the fact that the respondent has deserted the petitioner in April 2011 and lodged a false case against the petitioner, the marriage between them has been broken down irretrievably.

Hence, she seeks to allow the appeal by dissolving the marriage between the petitioner and the respondent on the grounds of cruelty and desertion.
7.

Per contra, Sri.B.Madhusudhan Adiga, learned counsel for the respondent supports the impugned judgment and decree of the Trial Court and submits that the allegations of cruelty and desertion have been clearly denied by the respondent in her statement of objections and evidence.

The respondent is always ready to lead the marital life with the petitioner, however, the petitioner is not ready and willing to take her back to the matrimonial home as he listens to the words of his family members.

It is submitted that the judgment of acquittal from the criminal case is not an honourable one but since the petitioner assured of compromise, the witnesses have not supported the case of prosecution which resulted in the acquittal of the case.
It is also submitted that the petitioner and his family members demanded dowry, harassed her and assaulted her.

Hence, two panchayats were Sri M N Ravikumar vs Smt Ningamma on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105862545/
3 convened.

sentences.text: RW-2 and RW-3 participated in the said panchayats and requested the petitioner to take back the respondent to the matrimonial home for which he had agreed.
However, later he turned around and filed the petition seeking decree for dissolution of marriage.
Hence, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.

8. On considering the submissions of both sides and on examining the materials on record, the point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether the Trial Court committed illegality in rejecting the petition of the appellant for divorce"?
ANALYSIS 9.
It is not in dispute that the marriage between the petitioner and respondent was solemnized on 06.06.2004 and during the wedlock, the couple were blessed with a son viz., Dhakshinamurthy.
The parties do not dispute that they have led married life from 06.06.2004 to April 2011.
It is also not in dispute that the petitioner is working as a Police Constable and the respondent is working as a Teacher in Government School.

10. The petitioner filed the petition seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty alleging that the respondent is an arrogant lady, does not adjust with the petitioner and his family members,
used to pick up quarrel on flimsy reasons, was in the habit of going to her parents house whenever she wanted and only on insistence of the petitioner she used to come back to matrimonial home.
Ultimately, in the month of April 2011, she deserted the petitioner and child and went back to her parents house and filed false complaint on 04.05.2011 alleging dowry harassment.
His employer has conducted departmental inquiry based on the registration of criminal complaint.
Both the proceedings have been closed, which clearly establishes cruelty and desertion by the respondent.

11. In support of the allegations of cruelty and desertion, the petitioner reiterated the pleading in his evidence and produced the certified copy of the judgment in C.C.No.517/2011 as Ex.P-4 and certified copy of the order passed by the Superintendent of Police, Ramanagara as Ex.P-6.
On re-appreciation of the entire pleading and evidence of the petitioner, it can be fairly said that the allegations of cruelty alleged are usual wear and tear of matrimonial life.

The allegation that the respondent was an arrogant lady, did not adjust with petitioner and family members and used to quarrel frequently,
cannot be accepted on its face value as the said statements are self-serving statements of PW-1 and are not corroborated with any other evidence.
PW-1, in his cross- examination, has clearly admitted that for more than six years he has led married life with respondent.
Admittedly, his family consists of other three members and they would have been the better persons to speak with regard to such alleged misconduct and cruelty of the respondent.
Petitioner has not offered any explanation for non-examination of his own family members.
It is specifically contended by the petitioner that the respondent has filed false criminal case against the petitioner and his family members which has resulted in honourable acquittal.
Similarly, the departmental inquiry proceedings initiated against the petitioner pursuant to the registration of criminal case also resulted in exoneration of the charges levelled against him.

Ex.P-4, the certified copy of the judgment in C.C.No.517/2011, shows Sri M N Ravikumar vs Smt Ningamma on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105862545/
4 that the accused therein were acquitted on the ground that the witnesses had not fully supported the case of the prosecution.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent claims that pending C.C.No.517/2011, a panchayat for reconciliation was held.
As per the terms of the said panchayat, to facilitate the acquittal of the accused, herself and her relative turned hostile, however, after acquittal, the petitioner did not take her back.
To prove that, she examined RWs-2 and 3, the mediators/panchayatdars.

12. Insofar as the exoneration of the petitioner from the departmental inquiry is concerned, the finding found at Ex.P-6 indicates that it is mainly based on the judgment of acquittal of the petitioner from the criminal proceedings.

Hence the contention urged by the petitioner that on the basis of a false complaint lodged by the respondent, a substantive enquiry was conducted and he has been exonerated from the charges leveled against him, has no merit for consideration and is accordingly rejected.
RWs-2 & 3 have deposed that during the panchayat the petitioner agreed to take back the respondent to matrimonial home, however, later he refused to take her back.
That shows due to the compromise, witnesses did not support the case of prosecution that lead to their acquittal.
Hence, the acquittal from the criminal proceedings is not an honourable acquittal.

The evidence of RWs-1 to 3 indicate that the respondent led the married life for nearly six years and due to some differences she was compelled to reside with her parents, hence, the same does not amount to desertion.
The above discussion shows that the allegation of cruelty and willful desertion was not proved.
13. For the above stated reasons, the Trial Court has rightly recorded the finding that there is no positive evidence led by the petitioner to prove the grounds of cruelty and desertion.
The said finding of the Trial Court is based on the pleading and evidence available on record and the same is neither perverse nor contrary to the material available on record.
The allegations of cruelty are very vague, neither any specific instances nor detailed particulars of cruelty by the respondent are pointed out in the pleading and in the evidence.
Hence, the material available on record are not sufficient to hold that the grounds of cruelty and desertion are proved to dissolve the marriage.
14. The allegation that the respondent left the matrimonial home in the month of April 2011 by deserting the petitioner and residing with her parents is not supported by any independent evidence.

The allegation of desertion is required to be pleaded properly and is required to be proved to the effect that the respondent has left the matrimonial home voluntarily with an intention to end the cohabitation permanently.

In the absence of any such evidence on record, mere statement that the respondent left the matrimonial home in the month of April 2011, which has been specifically denied by the respondent in her objections as well as evidence, cannot be accepted as the allegation of desertion is proved.

15. The Trial Court recorded the detailed findings and came to the right conclusion that the petitioner failed to prove the grounds of cruelty and desertion urged in the petition and dismissed the petition.
The said finding of the Trial Court is neither perverse nor contrary to the evidence on record calling for interference in the present appeal.

Hence, the following:
